result.title: EviSeek: An Evidence-Centric Agentic Framework for Embodied Active Information Seeking
result.summary: Active embodied question answering requires agents to acquire evidence through viewpoint changes and physical interaction. The central challenge is to avoid undirected interaction: taking plausible actions without specifying what evidence they should reveal for answering the question. Action plans and accumulated histories alone can leave the informational purpose of an interaction implicit. We introduce EviSeek, a training-free framework that makes question-derived evidence demands explicit acquisition objectives, linking observation-conditioned actions and selectively retained evidence to the information the agent seeks. On 3,436 ESI-Bench questions, EviSeek improves accuracy over the Single-model agent by 7.1 percentage points with Qwen3-VL-32B and 3.7 points with Gemini 3.1 Pro, while improving visual-support-weighted accuracy and reducing mean token usage. These findings support making the informational purpose of interaction explicit, with action selection and evidence retention organized around what the agent needs to learn to answer the question.

AI.brief_summary: 提出免训练的证据中心 agent 框架 EviSeek，把由问题导出的「证据需求」写成显式获取目标，用以驱动视角变换与物理交互动作，并选择性保留观测证据，在 ESI-Bench 的 3,436 题上提升了准确率与视觉支持加权准确率并降低平均 token 消耗。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接对应研究中「获取证据、视觉证据筛选、停止与动态计算」的关注点；其把交互的信息目的外显为目标的思路，可供核查能否用于 LVR 中判断 latent 状态缺少哪些视觉证据，而 token 下降究竟来自有效筛选还是启发式裁剪仍需读原文确认。
